.. py:function:: plot_histogram(x, bins='auto', density=False, xlabel='Amplitude', ylabel=None, title='Histogram', logy=False, grid=True, show_me=True)

   Plot a histogram of a signal.

   :param x: Input signal.
   :type x: array-like
   :param bins: Number of histogram bins or a NumPy histogram rule
                ("auto", "fd", "sturges", etc.).
   :type bins: int or str, default="auto"
   :param density: If True, plot probability density instead of counts.
   :type density: bool, default=False
   :param xlabel: Label for x-axis.
   :type xlabel: str
   :param ylabel: Label for y-axis. If None, uses "Count" or "Probability density".
   :type ylabel: str or None
   :param title: Figure title.
   :type title: str
   :param logy: Use logarithmic y-axis.
   :type logy: bool, default=False
   :param grid: Show grid.
   :type grid: bool, default=True


.. py:function:: plot_quantization_levels(x, title='Quantized Amplitude Levels', show_me=True)

.. py:function:: estimate_amplitude_bits(x: numpy.ndarray) -> Dict[str, Any]

   Estimate the number of bits required to represent the amplitudes
   of an already quantized signal.

   :param x: Input signal.
   :type x: ndarray

   :returns: Dictionary containing:
             - unique_levels
             - observed_bits
             - theoretical_bits
             - quantization_step
             - min_value
             - max_value
             - uniformly_quantized
   :rtype: dict


.. py:function:: plot_signal_outliers(x: numpy.typing.ArrayLike, x_no_outliers: numpy.typing.ArrayLike, mask: numpy.typing.ArrayLike, title: str = 'Signal with Outliers')

   Plot original signal and highlight the detected outliers,
   and also the interpolated signal after outlier removal.

   :param x: Input signal.
   :type x: array_like
   :param mask: Boolean array indicating the positions of the detected outliers.
   :type mask: array_like
   :param title: Title of the plot. Default is "Signal with Outliers".
   :type title: str, optional


.. py:function:: remove_outliers(input_signal: numpy.typing.ArrayLike, fs: float, win_ms: float = 200.0, k: float = 10.0, should_plot: bool = False) -> tuple[numpy.typing.NDArray[numpy.float64], numpy.typing.NDArray[numpy.bool_]]

   Remove impulsive amplitude outliers from a signal using a
   Hampel-like filter based on a moving median and median absolute
   deviation (MAD).

   Samples whose deviation from the local median exceeds ``k`` times
   the local robust standard deviation estimate are classified as
   outliers and replaced by values obtained through linear
   interpolation between neighboring valid samples. This preprocessing
   step is useful for suppressing large digitization artifacts before
   applying conventional filters.

   :param input_signal: Input signal.
   :type input_signal: array_like
   :param fs: Sampling frequency in Hz.
   :type fs: float
   :param win_ms: Length of the moving window in milliseconds used to estimate
                  the local median and MAD. The corresponding number of samples
                  is automatically rounded to the nearest odd integer.
                  Default is 200 ms.
   :type win_ms: float, optional
   :param k: Threshold multiplier applied to the local robust standard
             deviation estimate. Samples satisfying

                 abs(input_signal[n] - median[n]) > k * sigma[n]

             are considered outliers. Larger values make the detector less
             sensitive. Default is 6.0.
   :type k: float, optional

   :returns: * **y** (*ndarray*) -- Signal after replacing detected outliers by linear
               interpolation.
             * **mask** (*ndarray of bool*) -- Boolean array indicating the positions of the detected
               outliers. Elements equal to ``True`` correspond to samples
               that were replaced.

   .. rubric:: Notes

   The robust standard deviation estimate is computed as

   .. math::

       \sigma[n] = 1.4826 \, \mathrm{MAD}[n],

   where

   .. math::

       \mathrm{MAD}[n] = \mathrm{median}(|input_signal[n]-m[n]|),

   and :math:`m[n]` is the moving median.

   This method is particularly effective for removing isolated spikes
   caused by ADC errors, packet losses, or other impulsive artifacts,
   and it should generally be applied before bandpass filtering to
   avoid spreading the energy of the outliers over time.

   .. rubric:: Examples

   >>> x_clean, mask = remove_outliers(x, fs=500)
   >>> y = scipy.signal.filtfilt(b, a, x_clean)

   .. seealso::

      :obj:`scipy.signal.medfilt`
          Median filter.

      :obj:`numpy.interp`
          One-dimensional linear interpolation.
